Image fluency scores for several images at once

Source: R/fluency.R
img_fluency.Rd

img_fluency computes the image fluency scores for several images at once and returns the results as a data frame with one row per image.

Usage

img_fluency(
  imgs,
  metrics = c("contrast", "self_similarity", "simplicity", "symmetry"),
  gray = FALSE,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

imgs

Either a character vector with the paths to the image files (e.g., created by list.files() with full.names = TRUE) or a list of pre-loaded images (matrices or arrays of numeric values, e.g. by using img_read()).

metrics

Character vector that specifies which scores are computed. One or more of "contrast", "self_similarity", "simplicity", "symmetry", and "typicality". By default, all scores except typicality are computed (see details).

gray

logical. Should color images be converted into grayscale (using rgb2gray()) before the scores are computed? This speeds up the computation. (default: FALSE)

progress

logical. Should a progress bar be shown? (default: TRUE in interactive sessions)

Value

a data frame with one row per image (in the order of imgs). The first column filename contains the file names of the images (for a list of pre-loaded images: the names of the list; img1, img2, ... for images without a name). The other columns contain the scores and are named after metrics.

Details

The function reads one image after the other and computes the requested scores with the respective functions of the package using their default settings:

  • "contrast": img_contrast()

  • "self_similarity": img_self_similarity()

  • "simplicity": img_simplicity()

  • "symmetry": vertical symmetry, i.e., img_symmetry() with horizontal = FALSE

  • "typicality": img_typicality()

Typicality is not computed by default (but can be added to metrics) for two reasons. First, typicality is not a characteristic of a single image, but of an image relative to all other images that are analyzed. Thus, the typicality scores change if images are added or removed. Second, all images have to be kept in memory at the same time to compute typicality, which might be a problem if you analyze many or large images. For all other scores, only one image is kept in memory at a time.

The function does not stop if an image file cannot be read or if a score cannot be computed for an image (e.g., symmetry for an image without any variation in one image half). Instead, the respective scores in the results are NA, and a warning at the end lists the images concerned. Warnings of the individual functions are not shown. Use the individual functions if you need other than the default settings or want to find out why a score could not be computed for an image.

See also

img_read, img_contrast, img_self_similarity, img_simplicity, img_symmetry, img_typicality

Examples

# paths to some of the example images
files <- system.file("example_images", c("rails.jpg", "sky.jpg", "trees.jpg"),
                     package = "imagefluency")

# contrast and symmetry scores of all images
img_fluency(files, metrics = c("contrast", "symmetry"))
#>    filename   contrast  symmetry
#> 1 rails.jpg 0.36415048 0.9551137
#> 2   sky.jpg 0.08109417 0.6473722
#> 3 trees.jpg 0.18911031 0.1908871

# add typicality (of the images relative to each other)
img_fluency(files, metrics = c("contrast", "symmetry", "typicality"))
#>    filename   contrast  symmetry typicality
#> 1 rails.jpg 0.36415048 0.9551137  0.8910676
#> 2   sky.jpg 0.08109417 0.6473722  0.1035027
#> 3 trees.jpg 0.18911031 0.1908871  0.5195922

# all scores except typicality (default)
img_fluency(files)
#>    filename   contrast self_similarity simplicity  symmetry
#> 1 rails.jpg 0.36415048      -0.5784927  0.5357527 0.9551137
#> 2   sky.jpg 0.08109417      -1.5620177  0.5792614 0.6473722
#> 3 trees.jpg 0.18911031      -0.5505834  0.1045811 0.1908871
